title: Abbreviations
subtitle: MP, e.g., Dr, fridge, bike
summary: Understand the common abbreviations of written and spoken English, and the short forms of everyday words.

lesson.heading: Abbreviations you say as letters
rows: curriculum vitae (a history of your job experience)
lesson.note: A few abbreviations are said as a word, not as letters, for example **AIDS** and **PIN** (personal identification number, used with a bank or credit card).

lesson.heading: Asking about an abbreviation
lesson.text: To ask what an abbreviation means, use the phrasal verb **stand for**.

examples.text: *A:* What does *MP* **stand for**? *B:* Member of Parliament.

lesson.heading: Written only: you say the full word
Latin abbreviations in everyday English
rows: that's to say, in other words

lesson.heading: Shortened words
lesson.text: Many common words have a short form, especially in speech. Sometimes the short form is the normal one, and the full word sounds formal: *refrigerator*, *influenza*, *gymnasium* and *veterinary surgeon* are rare in conversation.

examples.text: It was warm, so I put the milk in the **fridge**.
The dog was sick, so we took her to the **vet**.
I was in bed all week with **flu**.
examples.note: influenza: an illness like a cold but more serious

examples.text: We did some experiments in the chemistry **lab**.
examples.note: laboratory: a special room where scientists work

lesson.heading: Abbreviations in letters, forms and messages
rows: at the bottom of a page
at the end of a letter, after your name

lesson.text: Use e.g. before an example and i.e. before an explanation: 'Bring warm clothes, e.g. a coat' but 'Bring warm clothes, i.e. not shorts'.

exercises.prompt: Match each abbreviation with its full form.

exercises.statement: ISP stands for Internet Service Player.
exercises.explanation: ISP stands for Internet Service Provider.
Correct. You may be asked for an ID card.

exercises.statement: MP stands for Minister of Parliament.
exercises.explanation: MP stands for Member of Parliament.

exercises.prompt: Match the written abbreviation with what it means.
Make it shorter: 'Olly had a mathematics examination this afternoon.' -> 'Olly had a maths ___ this afternoon.'
exercises.explanation: Exam is the short form of examination.

exercises.prompt: Make it shorter: 'Please help yourself to anything in the refrigerator.' -> '... anything in the ___.'
exercises.explanation: Fridge is the normal word; refrigerator sounds formal.

exercises.prompt: Make it shorter: 'My telephone number is next to the photographs.' -> 'My ___ number is next to the photos.'
exercises.explanation: Phone is the short form of telephone.

exercises.prompt: He didn't want to walk, so he went on his ___.
exercises.explanation: Bike is the short form of bicycle.

exercises.prompt: The dog was sick, so we had to take her to the ___.
exercises.explanation: A vet is a veterinary surgeon, an animal doctor.

exercises.prompt: When I sold my CDs, I put an ___ in the paper and had three replies the same day.
exercises.explanation: Ad and advert are both short for advertisement.

exercises.prompt: If you use the cashpoint, remember you'll need your ___ number.
exercises.explanation: PIN = personal identification number. It is said as a word.
We ask about an abbreviation with What does ... stand for?

exercises.prompt: Where would you normally see each abbreviation?
categories: On a form or a letter
In an email or text message

exercises.prompt: In that shop you can get books, pens, writing paper, ___
exercises.explanation: Etc. means and so on, at the end of a list.
